human_tolerance.notes: Since the 1960s it has moved into western towns and cities and around barns and houses, feeding at feedlots, grain elevators and landfills; fairly tolerant of people except where persecuted.

phases.name: nesting
phases.note: Both sexes build the large domed twig nest over 40-50 days, starting in February (later further north); old nests are repaired and reused.

phases.name: breeding
phases.note: Breeding starts in late March and ends in early July; clutch of six or seven eggs, incubation 16-21 days by the female alone, one brood usually, two if the first fails.

phases.name: young
phases.note: Young fly 3-4 weeks after hatching and feed with the adults for about two months before joining other juveniles.

phases.name: flocking
phases.note: Loose flocks outside the breeding season; birds roost communally each night in dense trees or shrubs, sometimes travelling long distances to reach the roost.

vocalizations.description: A quiet mix of croons, purrs, shrills and soft whistles around the nest, far less musical than most songbirds and easily missed.
The signature rapid 'ka-ka-ka-ka' chatter, sometimes preceded by 'skah-skah', given at predators and in mobbing and dominance disputes.

taxonomy.note: Described by Sabine in 1823 as Corvus Hudsonius; separated from Pica pica in 2000. GBIF usage key 5229487.

external.note: iNaturalist taxon id via Wikidata P3151 (143853), GBIF usage key via P846 (5229487), eBird code via P3444 (bkbmag1).

conservation.note: Wikidata P141 = least concern (Q211005); Wikipedia infobox Least Concern (IUCN 3.1).

range.note: Non-migratory western North America: Rocky Mountain states from New Mexico to Alaska, plus southern coastal Alaska, Yukon, British Columbia, Alberta, Saskatchewan, Manitoba and northwestern Ontario.

traits.note: Mass 0.179 kg is the midpoint of the documented span (females 141-179 g, males 167-216 g); mass_range is that full span. length_m 0.525 is the midpoint of 45-60 cm. wingspan_m 0.585 is the midpoint of 56-61 cm from the Italian Wikipedia article (the English one gives no wingspan), itself drawn from HBW. lifespan_y 6 from the lead (6-7 years wild) reconciled with the Breeding section (about 4-6 years). Diet shares are authored from the stated opportunistic omnivore diet (carrion, insects, seeds, berries, nuts, plus rodents, reptiles, amphibians, small birds and eggs; animal matter in summer, more vegetation in winter). Flock 3-30 and wariness 0.5 are authored from the described loose non-breeding flocks and 'fairly tolerant unless persecuted' wariness.

habitat.note: Walks and hops on the ground where it feeds, nests in trees (ground 0.7 / arboreal 0.3). Resource weights follow traits.diet plus the documented scavenging from predator kills; nest_platform and perch from the domed treetop nest and perching habits. Exploiter affinity and uses_gardens from the documented move into towns, feedlots and landfills since the 1960s.

seasonal.note: Nests built from February over 40-50 days; breeding late March to early July, clutch 6-7, incubation 16-21 days; young fly at 3-4 weeks and stay with adults about two months; loose winter flocks and communal roosts. ActiveYearRound because the species is generally non-migratory with only some winter movement. Egg duration 18 days is the midpoint of 16-21; juvenile 90 days combines nestling period and the roughly two months of post-fledging care, scale 0.6 authored.

vocalizations.note: Chatter description ('ka-ka-ka-ka', sometimes preceded by 'skah-skah') is quoted from the Vocalizations section; the song is the quieter croons, purrs, shrills and squawks also listed there. Season months, time windows and cooldowns are authored from the breeding season.

behavior.note: Authored parameters for the shared perching-songbird program: flees at 6 m (tolerant but wary where persecuted), forages on invertebrates as the main animal food, nesting window February to July to match nest building and breeding dates.

look.note: Colours from the Description section: largely black with white scapulars, belly and primaries, iridescent blue-green wings and tail, black bill and dark iris. Block proportions, the long-tail ratio (tail 230-320 mm) and exact hex values are authored judgement.
